text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Local companies, including those involved in small and medium scale industries were told to exploit fully the opportunities available in all areas of development in the Multimedia Super Corridor.
- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad assumed the chairmanship of the Group of 15 summit on Tuesday with a firm reminder that developing countries still had a lot to do to overcome global challenges.

- The government will now be more particular in classifying made-in-Malaysia components as many of them have been found to have very high foreign child-parts content. Child parts are the basic items that go into making larger components.
- Downside factors experienced by Tenaga Nasional Bhd in the first half have not gone away and may prove to be a further drag on the utility's results for the full financial year ended August 31.
- Authorities are still trying to trace the owner of the double-storey house in Petaling Jaya where three brothers and a microbiologist were killed in a fire on Monday.
